transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… what brings me in is this thing I’ve been having with elevators, mostly slow ones, and small rooms where the door locks or feels like it’s locked. The moment I step in, it’s like my chest jumps right away, before I’ve even had time to tell myself anything sensible. I just get this strong urge to get back out, like I need to leave immediately, and for a few seconds I can’t really think straight. It comes on so fast that it catches me off guard, even though I sort of know it might happen.
Do these feelings of panic only happen in elevators or small rooms, or do you also experience them in other situations where you might not expect them?

It’s really those situations, mostly. The slow elevators, especially if they sort of crawl between floors, and then those small rooms where the door shuts and it feels locked, even if maybe it’s just a regular door. That’s when it hits me right away.

I mean, I’ll step in and before I can even tell myself, “Now don’t be foolish, it’s just an elevator,” my chest kind of jumps and I get this strong feeling like, “Get out, get out now.” It’s not like I sit there thinking about it first and then work myself up. It comes on almost immediately, and for a few seconds I don’t think straight at all. I’m just focused on needing to leave.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that came out of the blue, even when you weren’t in a situation like an elevator or a small room?

No… I don’t think so. Not like that, anyway. I mean, I can get startled or worried like anybody, but the real sudden fear I’m talking about seems to be tied to those places where I feel shut in. I haven’t noticed it just happening while I’m sitting at home or walking around or doing some ordinary thing. It’s when I’m in that sort of enclosed situation that it comes on so fast.

When you feel that panic coming on in the elevator or a small room, do you find yourself avoiding those places altogether, or trying to endure them with great difficulty because you're so worried about having another attack?

Yes… I do avoid them, more than I like to admit. These days I’ll take the stairs if I can, even if it’s slower or a little hard on me. I tell myself it’s good exercise, but honestly a lot of the time it’s because I don’t want to get in the elevator and have that feeling start up.

And there are places I’ll sort of work around. At the museum, if there’s something in the archives or one of those tight little rooms, I’ll pass on it if I can. I feel a bit foolish saying that, because it’s not like I don’t understand the door opens and people use those places all the time. But if I picture myself being closed in there, I start thinking, no, better not.

If I can’t avoid it, I try to make it so somebody is nearby. Like I might ask a friend to wait outside or stay close, just so I know there’s someone there if I need to come out. It embarrasses me some, being my age and still needing that kind of reassurance, but it makes it easier to get through.
Have you ever felt sudden, overwhelming panic or fear in situations where you weren’t in an enclosed space or worried about being trapped?

No, not really. I don’t get that kind of sudden, overwhelming panic just out of nowhere, as far as I can tell. It’s more when I step into one of those places — a slow elevator, especially, or a little room where the door shuts and feels locked. That’s when my chest sort of jumps right away, and I get this strong need to get back out before I can even think properly.

It’s not like I’m sitting in a chair at home and suddenly it comes over me. It’s tied to that feeling of being closed in or maybe not being able to get out quickly. Then it happens almost before I’ve had time to reason with myself.
Have you ever experienced a panic attack in a situation where you weren't feeling enclosed or trapped, such as being outdoors, in a crowd, or at home?

No, I can’t really say I have. I’m trying to think it through, because I don’t want to answer too quick and miss something, but… no. If I’m outdoors, or at home, or just around people, I don’t remember having that same kind of panic come over me for no reason.

It’s the being shut in, or thinking I might not be able to get out easy, that seems to set it off. If that piece isn’t there, then I may feel nervous about ordinary things now and then, but not that sudden, overwhelming fear like with the enclosed places.
Have you ever experienced a panic attack in open spaces, public places, or while you were not near an exit, where you felt sudden and intense fear without being in an enclosed or trapped situation?

No, I don’t think it’s happened that way. Not in open places or just being out in public, anyway. It’s really that closed-in feeling that does it.

Like I was saying, what brings me in is more when I step into a slow elevator, or one of those small rooms where the door shuts and I get the idea it might be locked or hard to open. My chest jumps right away, almost like my body reacts before my head can catch up, and then I get this strong need to get back out. I’m not standing there calmly thinking it through — it just comes on fast, and I want out before I can even think straight.

If I’m somewhere open and I can see where to go, or I’m not feeling shut in, then I don’t get that same sudden fear. It’s really the elevator or little locked room kind of situation.

Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or panic when you weren’t in an enclosed space or worried about being trapped — for example, if you saw a certain animal, were on a plane, or encountered another specific situation that might upset you?

No, I don’t think so. I’m trying to run through those examples you gave — animals, planes, things like that — and nothing really comes to mind where I had that sudden panic just from seeing something or being in some other situation.

I mean, there are things I don’t especially like, same as anybody, but I wouldn’t say I get that rush of fear or panic from an animal or anything like that. If it’s not about being closed in or feeling like I can’t get out, then I haven’t noticed that same kind of reaction.
